paper.title: GenEnv: Difficulty-Aligned Co-Evolution Between LLM Agents and Environment Simulators
paper.central_claim: Difficulty-aligned co-training of an agent and environment simulator improves downstream agent performance and data efficiency relative to static/untargeted synthetic training.

provenance.notes: Configured execution identity gpt-6.1-sol supplied by dispatch; no independently exposed model receipt/session identifier. No model probing.

evidence.support_explanation: Agent is a learned policy; scope supported with full update descriptions in E002/E003.

evidence.quote: we instantiate this using Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO)
We then construct a weighted SFT set of environment generations and fine-tune
evidence.support_explanation: Environment improvement also resides in model weights, not editable harness.

evidence.quote: so the agent can (i) learn from fresh on-policy experiences and (ii) retain mastery of earlier curricula by continuing to sample from the accumulated pool.
evidence.support_explanation: Persisted data are training pools, not a deployed non-weight learning artifact.

evidence.quote: We do not attach additional multi-agent orchestration or human-in-the-loop corrections to any method, to focus the comparison on training and data regimes.
evidence.support_explanation: Evaluation targets training and data regimes.

evidence.quote:
GenEnv-Static:
We use the
generate_static_augmentation.py
script to pre-generate 5 variations for each of the 544 original training samples, resulting in a fixed dataset of 3,264 samples. The agent is trained using standard PPO for 10 epochs.
evidence.support_explanation: Static comparator differs in optimizer, but no score assigned because scope exclusion.

reason: Frozen rubric A3: agent GRPO and simulator RWR/SFT both update weights. Persisted pools support subsequent weight training, not a non-weight harness artifact used by a frozen agent; H22 taxonomy membership does not override scope.
